records.name: Theater of Witness
records.summary: A testimonial theater group that turns true stories from people whose voices are often overlooked into plays and films, which the storytellers perform themselves.
records.what_you_do: Go to a performance or film screening. Storytellers and community members can also take part in productions, and the group offers a way to book screenings.

schedule.text: Productions and screenings are scheduled as events. The GrandWomen run was June 11 to 13, 2026 at the Suzanne Roberts Theatre.

cost.text: Ticket prices were not listed on the group's site

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to the next performance, or email the group to book a screening of Grand Young Women
first_step.basis: Public performances are open to anyone, and the site gives a direct email to book a screening

records.notes: The group's own site has no dated events; the June 2026 GrandWomen run comes from a press listing and ticketing page. The .com address redirects to .org. The phone number on the site is not verified for this group. The mailing list link on the site is malformed. Dated archive entry July 2023.

records.name: Theatre in the X
records.summary: A free theater company in West Philadelphia that stages productions for the African American community and gives chances to playwrights, actors, directors, and behind-the-scenes crew.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free production. You can also audition, volunteer, or work with the group, such as in stage crew, sound, or DJ roles, through the form on the website.

schedule.text: Show dates are not listed on the site; check the website for the next production

first_step.how: Fill in the audition, volunteer, or work with us form on the website, or sign up for the mailing list
first_step.basis: Free public shows and an open form to get involved, but no dated events are listed to see what it is like

records.notes: The site shows two productions and a production history page but no dates. Email is published only as obscured text on the page, so none is recorded. The group's stated community focus is recorded as a heritage tag from its own description. No dated evidence found in one site check.

records.name: TILT Institute for the Contemporary Image
records.summary: A photography center in North Philadelphia that runs gallery shows, printing services, artist residencies, and youth education for photographers and image makers at every level.
records.what_you_do: Visit the gallery and its free events, take a tutorial or use the Artist Lab printing team, join a youth program, or apply for an artist residency.

schedule.text: Gallery open Wednesday to Saturday, 12 to 6 pm. Exhibitions run September to November 2026 and December 2026 to February 2027, with an October 2026 talk.

cost.text: Gallery visits and events are listed on the calendar. Tutorials, printing, and memberships have fees; exact prices were not checked.

first_step.how: Visit the gallery on a Wednesday to Saturday afternoon, or sign up for the newsletter to hear about the next opening
first_step.basis: The gallery and public events are open to anyone, with a clear calendar and a membership option, though some tutorials are paid

records.notes: Volunteer opportunities are not listed. Youth programs are listed on the menu without details. InVISION 26 appears on the menu with no date. Feedback form on the site.

records.name: Tiny Farm Wagon
records.summary: A mobile art classroom and greenhouse run by CultureTrust that uses art and gardening to celebrate and support wellness in Black life and culture.
records.what_you_do: Visit the garden in person, read about the Mother Tongue public art series, or join the newsletter for workshop and event news. Workshops and events are planned around the wagon and the garden.

schedule.text: No dates or schedule are listed on the site

cost.text: Not listed on the site; the donation page is separate

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter at tinyfarmwagon.org, or email the group to ask when the garden is open to visitors
first_step.basis: The page invites visits and newsletter sign-ups but lists no dates, so the way in is unclear

records.notes: Working site with no dates. The newsletter form notes that its storage is not set up. A search found no 2026 dates. The zip for the address is 19104 on this site but 19107 on Theater of Witness's site, so the zip is left out. Parent is CultureTrust of Greater Philadelphia; a donation-focused mirror site was seen in search and not used as a source.

records.name: University Community Collaborative
records.summary: A Temple University program that runs media and storytelling classes for Philadelphia high school students, helping them build leadership skills and a voice in their communities.
records.what_you_do: High school students apply to a youth media program (POPPYN, POWER, or VOICES) and learn filmmaking, public speaking, and project work in a team. Organizations can also learn youth leadership and media literacy from the group.

schedule.text: Youth programs run through the school year; applications for 2026 to 2027 are open now

cost.text: Fees are not listed on the page; donations are accepted

first_step.how: Apply through the Apply Now page at uccollab.org/apply
first_step.basis: Youth programs need an application before a student sees what the program is like

records.notes: The site says applications for the 2026 to 2027 school year are open now, but its announcements have no dates, so status is probably_active rather than active. Program names POPPYN, POWER, and VOICES are listed by the group. No volunteer or drop in events are listed.

records.name: Very Good Dance Theatre
records.notes: A dance theatre company whose site is under construction, with content coming soon. The only public ways in are donation and social media links. No class, membership, volunteer, or community program is listed, so it is recorded as not_a_group under the arts company rule. Revisit when the site is live.

records.name: Vox Populi Gallery
records.summary: An artist-run gallery in North Chinatown that hosts exhibitions, performances, film screenings, and community events, and runs open calls and space rentals for artists.
records.what_you_do: Come to an exhibition opening, performance, or screening. Artists can apply to open calls, and members can join the Vox Circle or the board.

schedule.text: Exhibitions and events run through October and November 2026, with an opening reception in October and a screening in November. Open calls and rentals run through the year.

cost.text: Some events are ticketed, for example a $15 October party. Other event prices were not checked.

first_step.how: Come to an October or November opening or event, or sign up for the mailing list; open calls are another way in
first_step.basis: Public exhibitions and events have a clear calendar and a mailing list, but no beginner program is listed

records.notes: Recent August 2026 open calls and Fringe productions are also on the site. No classes or specific volunteer program listed. Board recruitment announced without a date.

records.name: Weirdo LLC
records.notes: The site is for WEIRDO, an arts event with a separate Queer Circus Fest, presented by the East Kensington Arts Committee. Event pages are dated only by year (2021 to 2024 and 2026). There are no classes, volunteer roles, or membership listed, and the public way in is attending the event, so it is recorded as not_a_group. The East Kensington Arts Committee is listed in leads_only for a separate check. Contact email published on the site was not recorded.

records.name: West Philly Bizarre
records.summary: A nonprofit makers market that gives local artists, crafters, and culture creators low-cost or free places to sell, mostly for West Philadelphians from underserved communities.
records.what_you_do: Shop or sell at the Clark Park market on select Saturdays, take a workshop such as the spring nail class, or apply as a vendor. First-time vendors from Southwest and West Philly get priority at Clark Park.

schedule.text: Clark Park market on select Saturdays, April through November. Pop-ups and workshops are announced on the events calendar.

cost.text: A $15 contribution pays for one vendor table at Clark Park. A spring 2026 nail workshop cost $45.

first_step.how: Visit the Clark Park market on a Saturday, or sign up for the newsletter to hear when vendor applications open in late winter
first_step.basis: The market and workshops are open to anyone, and the site explains how first-time vendors apply

records.notes: The spring pop-up is dated April 1 to June 7, 2026; the site does not state the year, so 2026 is inferred from the workshop date on the same page. The Clark Park address is not published on the site. Vendor applications are currently closed. Contact is via a contact page, so no email or phone is recorded. The group name in the batch includes CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia; the site describes itself as a 501(c)(3).

records.name: Writers Room
records.summary: Drexel University's literary arts program for students, alumni, and neighbors, offering free readings, workshops, a writing course, and community storytelling projects.
records.what_you_do: Attend a free event from the calendar, join the mailing list for workshops and exhibitions, or enroll in the WRIT290 writing course. Community programs such as Crossing Streets link West Philadelphia and Chinatown.

schedule.text: Upcoming events are on the calendar page; the site lists no dates

cost.text: Free; programs are open to anyone

first_step.how: Sign up for the mailing list, or check the calendar and attend the next free event
first_step.basis: Free public events with a mailing list, but no dated events are listed to see what it is like

records.notes: Working site with programs (Second Tuesday, Tripod, Seeding Joy, Unmapping, Crossing Streets, WRIT290) but no dated events. The page footer year is not treated as evidence. Second Story Collective is named as a partner and is not checked; it could be a lead.

leads_only.name: East Kensington Arts Committee
leads_only.note: named as the presenter of WEIRDO and Queer Circus Fest on the WEIRDO site, not checked on its own page

leads_only.name: Second Story Collective
leads_only.note: named as a partner on the Writers Room site with a new house, no own URL found, not checked

notes: Theater of Witness: the .com address redirects to .org; the .org site had no dated events, so the June 2026 run was taken from a press listing and ticketing page. Tiny Farm Wagon and Writers Room have working sites with no dates, so they are probably_active with low confidence. A search turned up a donation-focused mirror of Tiny Farm Wagon that was not used as a source. Two WebSearch calls used of 2; 11 WebFetch calls used. Budget not exhausted.
